title: Knowledge check: Introduction to jQuery Effects

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of introduction to jquery effects?
options: Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
Built-in effects and .animate() can reveal state changes, but effects should not block interaction or ignore reduced-motion preferences. Prefer CSS transitions for simple visual changes.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: Built-in effects and .animate() can reveal state changes, but effects should not block interaction or ignore reduced-motion preferences. Prefer CSS transitions for simple visual changes.
questions.explanation: Built-in effects and .animate() can reveal state changes, but effects should not block interaction or ignore reduced-motion preferences. Prefer CSS transitions for simple visual changes. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.
